cr_data.provenance: (An American Place, New York, NY); (The Downtown Gallery, New York, NY); Wright Ludington, Santa Barbara, California, 1934; Richard L. Feigen & Co., New York, NY, and Hirschl & Adler Galleries, Inc., New York, NY, 1981; (Hirschl & Adler Galleries, Inc., New York, NY) (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Sold to Wright Ludington." Pictured in 1933 New York (An American Place) Stieglitz installation photograph. Whitney Archive and Abiquiú Notebooks associate it with no. 14 in this exhibition, but arrangement of pictures in the Stieglitz photograph and titles on the checklist identify it as no. 7; see Appendix III, figure 54. See cat. nos. 806–9. Reproduced and titled *White Barn, Canada* in *Abstract & Surrealist Art in America* (1944). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A white barn with a black pitched roof and two large black entrances stands on a strip of flat green earth. A small black door and window stand at the far left of the barn. Above the structure is a clear blue sky.
imageCaption: Image courtesy of a scanned transparency made for Georgia O'Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné. This image has not been color proofed and may differ from the original. It will be replaced when newer photography becomes available.
